result:
The A20 pagination defect is fixed and every acceptance check passes, including the full integration run. The 1,000-initiative register now returns every row exactly once. Changes are uncommitted, as asked.

**Root cause.** It wasn't the missing tiebreaker the assignment suspected; the order already ended in `id`. When no `sort` is given, the initiative list orders by `updated_at desc, id desc`. Its cursor stored `updated_at` as a JS `Date` (millisecond precision), but PostgreSQL keeps microseconds. So the next page skipped any row that shared the page's last millisecond with a smaller microsecond. That's why one row was lost only under load: fast inserts land in the same millisecond. BE-R had already found this case and left it marked as an expected failure (`it.fails`); that test now passes normally.

**Fix.**
- **Helper:** a new one in `platform/cursor.ts` reads the timestamp key from PostgreSQL with all six fractional digits and compares it as a timestamp. Cursors issued before the fix are still accepted. A malformed timestamp or id in a cursor now gets a 400 instead of reaching the database.
- **Where:** applied to the initiative list and to 16 other lists with the same defect: T08 dependencies, business cases, benefit formulas, calculations, selections, funding, resource demands, overrides, dispensations, procedure instances, both draft lists, integration runs, imports and outbound writes, and operational exceptions.
- **BE-V and BE-R lists:** I checked all of them and their order was already total, so I left them alone. The same goes for webhooks, which sort and compare on the same millisecond value.
- **Visible change:** only the opaque `nextCursor` string changes. Items, order and the filter hash are byte-identical to DG5. The contract calls the cursor opaque, so there's no contract change, no migration and no new dependency.

**Tests.**
- **New test** (`cursor-microsecond-ties.test.ts`, 12 cases): 240 initiatives and 240 dependencies inside one millisecond, 84 of them sharing exactly the same timestamp. It is deterministic. With the old cursor temporarily put back, it lost rows every time (only 84, 89, 108 and 180 of 240 came back at page sizes 1, 7, 25 and 100). With the fix, all 12 cases pass.
- **BE-R's golden test:** I updated it to expect the microsecond cursor.
- **QA test:** not edited.

| Check | Exit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `validate.mjs --historical --stage DG5` (start and end) | 0 | PASS |
| `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm -r build`, `pnpm lint`, prettier check, `pnpm openapi:lint` | 0 each | — |
| `pnpm test`, locale unset and `C.UTF-8` | 0 / 0 | unit-node 186 files / 2,803 tests; unit-web 120 / 2,015; nocodegen 3 / 259 passed, 2 skipped (same in both) |
| Full `pnpm test:integration` | 0 | 407/407 files; 4,131 passed, 1 skipped, 2 todo. A20 4/4 |

Two runs exited non-zero, both disclosed in the handback:
- **Targeted integration run:** my own fixture SQL had a syntax error, so the new test's 12 cases were skipped. I fixed it and they passed alone.
- **Old-cursor run:** deliberate, to prove the new test catches the defect.

No pinned count changed. No operations were routed, so there's no change to any pending list, and no user-facing text was made untrue.

**For you to decide or know:**
- **Missing section:** `p6-work-split.md` has no "pre-freeze repair: register pagination loses a row" section. I worked from the assignment text and the BE-R and BE-V sections.
- **Merge conflicts:** 17 of the changed files are outside BE-R's and BE-V's named lines. The edits there are small and mechanical, but expect minor conflicts if another task has touched those list queries.
- **Coverage gap:** the new deterministic test covers only initiatives and dependencies. The other 15 repaired lists rely on their existing tests.
- **ADR note:** ADR-0057 §5's "byte-identical" rule no longer holds for the cursor's bytes. I don't own the ADR, so the proposed note text is in the handback.

Everything is in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG6/`:
- T-DG6-BE-X7-backend-workflow-engineer.md (the handback)
- T-DG6-BE-X7-evidence/ (the logs)
